title: Simple harmonic motion
summary: Oscillations where acceleration is proportional to displacement and directed towards equilibrium: period, frequency, the mass–spring system and simple pendulum, and (HL) phase, equations of motion and energy in SHM.

keyterms.definition: Oscillation in which acceleration is proportional to displacement from equilibrium and directed towards it: a = −ω²x.
The position where the resultant force on an oscillator is zero.
The maximum displacement from the equilibrium position, x₀.
Time for one complete oscillation, T = 1/f.
Number of oscillations per unit time, in hertz.
Having a period that does not depend on the amplitude, a property of SHM.
A force that always acts towards the equilibrium position.
The angle φ in x = x₀ sin(ωt + φ) describing where an oscillator is in its cycle at t = 0.
Total energy E_T = ½mω²x₀², constantly interchanged between kinetic and potential energy.

lessons.title: Conditions for SHM and the period

questions.prompt: Which condition defines simple harmonic motion?
options: Acceleration is proportional to displacement and opposite in direction
questions.explanation: SHM requires a = −ω²x: a restoring acceleration proportional to displacement.

questions.text: An oscillator completes 20 oscillations in 8.0 s. Its period is ___ s.

questions.statement: In SHM the speed is greatest at the equilibrium position.
questions.explanation: All energy is kinetic at x = 0, so speed is maximum there; it is zero at the amplitude.

questions.prompt: Where is the magnitude of acceleration greatest for an object in SHM?
questions.explanation: |a| = ω²|x| is largest when |x| = x₀.

questions.prompt: A mass on a spring has period 1.0 s. The mass is replaced by one four times larger. The new period is
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(m/k), so T ∝ √m: four times the mass doubles the period.

questions.text: A simple pendulum of length 2.45 m on Earth (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) has a period of about ___ s.

questions.prompt: Match each quantity to its expression.
questions.explanation: These SHM relations are in the data booklet; know when each applies.

questions.statement: A pendulum’s period depends on the mass of the bob.
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(L/g) contains no mass: a heavier bob needs more force but has proportionally more inertia.

questions.prompt: Why is the simple pendulum only approximately simple harmonic?
options: Its restoring force is proportional to sin θ, not θ, so SHM holds only for small angles
questions.explanation: For small angles sin θ ≈ θ (in radians), giving a ∝ −x.

questions.prompt: Order the positions of a pendulum bob starting from release at one extreme, over half a cycle.
items: Maximum displacement on the other side
questions.explanation: Kinetic and potential energy swap twice per full cycle.

lessons.title: Phase, equations and energy in SHM

questions.prompt: For SHM with x = x₀ sin ωt, the velocity is
questions.explanation: Differentiating x = x₀ sin ωt gives v = ωx₀ cos ωt.

questions.text: An oscillator with ω = 4.0 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.050 m has maximum speed ___ m s⁻¹.

questions.prompt: An oscillator with ω = 5.0 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.10 m is at x = 0.060 m. What is its speed?

questions.statement: Two oscillators with a phase difference of π rad move in opposite directions at every instant.
questions.explanation: A phase difference of π (antiphase) means one is at +x when the other is at −x, with opposite velocities.

questions.prompt: If the amplitude of an SHM oscillator doubles (same ω and mass), its total energy
questions.explanation: E_T = ½mω²x₀², so E ∝ x₀².

questions.text: A 0.20 kg mass oscillates with ω = 10 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.10 m. Its total energy is ___ J.

questions.prompt: Match each position to the energy statement.
questions.explanation: E_p = ½mω²x², so E_p = ½E_T when x² = x₀²/2.

questions.prompt: An oscillator starts at its maximum positive displacement at t = 0. Which equation describes it?
questions.explanation: cos 0 = 1, so x = x₀ at t = 0; equivalently x = x₀ sin(ωt + π/2).

questions.statement: In SHM, velocity leads displacement by a phase of π/2.
questions.explanation: If x = x₀ sin ωt then v = ωx₀ cos ωt = ωx₀ sin(ωt + π/2).

questions.prompt: On a graph of kinetic energy against time for an SHM oscillator of period T, the KE varies with period
questions.explanation: KE is maximum each time the oscillator passes equilibrium, twice per cycle, so its period is T/2.
